title: Bakery and Postcard
premise: Marine biologist Hazel Villalobos returns to her coastal hometown for a family reunion, dreading the questions about her failed engagement, and recruits Theo Marchetti — the boy who once left her at the last train station to honor his family's obligations — to pose as her boyfriend. Their fake date rekindles everything they buried, but Theo is hiding that he's back in town only briefly, sent to sell his late grandmother's bakery, the very postcard-perfect place where Hazel's memories live. As Hazel fights to save the bakery and Theo's family pressures him to close the deal, loyalty to family collides with the truth of what they still feel. At the reunion's end, Hazel must decide whether to let him stay after the last train leaves; Theo chooses her, keeps the bakery open, and they begin an honest second chance as partners in love and in bread.
about_author: Noor Ravensworth is the pen name of a former pastry chef turned novelist who writes love stories set in small coastal towns where food carries memory. She lives by the sea with her partner, two rescue dogs, and a sourdough starter older than their relationship.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Returning home for the Villalobos family reunion, Hazel counts sea turtle nests instead of answering questions about her broken engagement. Her mother announces a plus-one is expected. The emotional beat: guarded loneliness disguised as competence, ending with Hazel impulsively claiming she's bringing someone.

chapters.title: The Boy at the Station
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hunting for a fake date, Hazel runs into Theo Marchetti restocking his grandmother's shuttered bakery. Ten years ago he left on the last train without saying goodbye. He agrees to play her boyfriend; she doesn't ask why he's really in town. Beat: old wounds wrapped in easy banter.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner, Unrehearsed Hearts
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo meets the loud, loving Villalobos clan and realizes the fake date feels dangerously real by dessert. His phone buzzes with reminders from his family's property firm: the bakery sale closes in two weeks. Beat: warmth he doesn't deserve, guilt tightening like a knot.

chapters.title: Postcards from Before
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Cleaning the bakery's back room, Hazel finds a shoebox of unsent postcards Theo wrote her after he left — every one addressed, none mailed. When he catches her reading, the truth of his silence surfaces partially. Beat: tenderness curdling into hurt; the past refuses to stay boxed.

chapters.title: Salt and Proofing Dough
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A dawn baking session becomes confession-adjacent: Theo admits he left because his father gave him an ultimatum — family duty or Hazel. They almost kiss, interrupted by the buyer's surveyor photographing the bakery. Beat: hope rising like dough, then deflating under cold reality.

chapters.title: The Reunion Tide
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the reunion's beach bonfire, Hazel's ex-fiancé appears, and Theo defends her with a conviction that fools no one, least of themselves. Hazel's aunt privately warns Theo not to break her heart twice. Beat: jealousy and protectiveness expose the fake date as anything but.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel discovers the sale contract in Theo's bag — he was sent to close the deal on the bakery, her sanctuary, and never told her. Confrontation on the pier: loyalty versus truth, both bleeding. Beat: betrayal, sharp and salt-bitter; she walks away before he can explain.

chapters.title: Last Train Leaving
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts his father and tears up the sale agreement, choosing truth over duty for the first time. But Hazel has gone to the station to leave early, unable to face the reunion's final night. Beat: desperation, a race against a departure board, and a choice hanging.

chapters.title: Stay After the Whistle
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the platform, Theo asks Hazel to let him stay after the last train leaves — no more postcards, no more leaving. She makes him say the true thing out loud, all of it, before she takes his hand. Beat: climax; vulnerability finally outruns pride.

chapters.title: Bakery and Postcard
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Weeks later, the bakery reopens under both their names, its walls papered with Theo's ten years of unsent postcards, finally delivered. Hazel mails one last card herself — to future them. Beat: resolution; second chances aren't about timing, but about staying.
